title: FEAT: Expose per-route model health (primary vs fallback)
author: gggff123
pr_body_excerpt:
Fixes #14897

- Adds a cached `/v1/models/status/routes` endpoint and Tinybird pipe containing caller-visible model totals alongside every observed primary/fallback route.
- Adds expandable route rows, rescue counts, and a Primary off badge to the monitor while preserving caller-visible headline health.
- Records upstream attempt duration separately from full request duration so fallback latency excludes earlier failures. Historical rows without attempt timing are excluded from route latency. Documents both counting grains and timing semantics.
- Validation: 71 tracking tests, 18 monitor tests, 2 OpenAPI tests, TypeScript, Biome, and synthetic ClickHouse checks for rescued requests and missing historical timing.
- Staging: Tinybird deployment 146 is active and verified through the endpoint and local dashboard, including counts, rescue failures, and attempt latency. Production datasource/pipe deployment is required before monitor rollout. Configured-but-unused routes and provider/region visibility remain follow-ups.

Closes #14860

gist.headline: Routes Learn to Self-Report
gist.blurb: The model monitor can now show which routes are thriving, which ones called for backup, and how long each upstream attempt actually took. Even fallback paths deserve honest weather reports.
gist.summary: Added the cached `/v1/models/status/routes` endpoint and Tinybird route-health pipe, exposing caller-visible totals, primary-versus-fallback routes, rescue counts, and per-attempt upstream latency that excludes time spent on earlier failed attempts.
gist.impact: Developers and operators can now inspect route-level model health in the monitor, expand routes to see primary and fallback behavior, and compare accurate fallback attempt latency without historical rows lacking attempt timing skewing the result.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy route-health garden: individual model routes are flowering paths leading from a primary gate to a helpful fallback gate, with tiny timing clocks and a rescue-count signpost. Polli, wearing a small observability headset and carrying a clipboard, watches the paths while the CRT Monitor Robot enthusiastically displays a healthy route map; code-plants and flowers make the technical dashboard feel alive.
